items.title: Reveal Mechanisms for Padlock-Free Escape Rooms!
items.description: Escape Rooms are synonymous with padlocks; the satisfying mechanical "clunk" as the shackle releases in your hand both confirms that you solved a puzzle correctly, and also grants access to your reward! But they have become so widely-used that players have become somewhat saturated and bored by them; with many players now actively seeking out experiences that use more advanced alternatives to reveal content with more theatrical effect. In this video, I'll demonstrate some lock, release, and reveal mechanisms - Electromagnetic locks, solenoid catches, linear actuators, and pneumatic cylinders - each with their own advantages and disadvantages. items.title: Arduino Logic Puzzle Deduction Board
items.description: In this video, I'll explain how I created a physical electronic "deduction board" logic puzzle game inspired by games such as Cluedo (Clue) and The Traitors, in which players must eliminate suspects using logical deduction until only one valid solution remains. It uses an Arduino Nano, 15x arcade buttons, a DY-SV5W MP3 player module, 3x PCF8574 port expanders to read the button inputs, and 3x TPIC6B595 power shift registers to drive the LED lamps. I also added a relay that can deactivate a maglock when the puzzle is solved, making it suitable for use in escape rooms, for example. items.title: Node-RED + QLC+ Automated Event-Driven Show Control for Escape Rooms and Theatre
items.description: Learn how to use Node-RED and QLC+ together to build an event-driven show control system for escape rooms, theatre, interactive installations, themed attractions, and automated lighting effects. Node-RED handles the input, logic, sensors, timers, and state, while QLC+ handles the lighting design, addressing DMX fixtures, and cue playback. This approach is especially useful for non-linear show control, where cues do not always happen in a fixed order. For example, an escape room puzzle might be solved at any time, a sensor might trigger unexpectedly, or an operator might need to override the system manually. You can download the software from the following sources. They are both open-source and 100% free, but please do consider supporting the creators if you find them useful!: - https://nodered.org/ - https://www.qlcplus.org/ Timings: 00:00:00 - 00:03:59 Introduction 00:04:00 - 00:14:09 QLC+ 00:14:10 - 00:22:18 Node-RED 00:22:19 - 00:23:06 Conclusion Join the Discord server at https://discord.gg/9GxCdkaAC #NodeRED #QLCPlus #DMXLighting #EscapeRoom #Tech #Automation #InteractiveInstallation #MQTT

items.title: Build your own ESP32 DMX Lighting and Sound Controller for under $15!
items.description: In this video I'll explain how to build your own scene-based DMX lighting and audio controller using an ESP32, a DY-SV5W MP3 Module, and an RS485 Transceiver module. Scenes can be cued on a simple linear playlist, advanced automatically after a specified duration, or when triggered by a manual input, sensor, or control message received over a network. Perfect for haunted houses, escape rooms, and other interactive experiences that you want to introduce more theatrical lighting. items.title: Stop Hard-Coding LED Animations! Upgrade from Arduino/ESP32 → sACN + WLED
items.description: Many of my projects and escape room puzzles use Arduino or ESP32 to control WS2812B LEDs using FastLED. That works for simple direct effects, but it doesn't scale to room-scale lighting, and limits the possibilites for more complex animations and effects. In this video, I explain how to move from hard-coded RGB values to a more professional theatre-style lighting system, where lighting effects can be manipulated in realtime and streamed as DMX data over Ethernet using sACN (E1.31). I'll be demonstrating this using free software like QLC+, xLights, or Jinx! to send the sACN data which is then received on an ESP32 running WLED. Instead of reflashing firmware onto a microprocessor every time you want a lighting change, this means you can: - Create complex animations (up to 40,000 LEDs) - Scaled across multiple rooms - Synchronised between fixtures - Manipulated in realtime from one PC This is the next step for Escape room owners, DIY/holiday lighting builders, theatre tech enthusiasts, and beginners to pixel mapping, and it opens up possibilities for even more impressive, more immersive, createive lighting effects. More details about all of the projects featured on this channel can be found at Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/c/playfultech And you can join the discussion on the Discord: https://discord.gg/76kDFjuZ

items.title: Make "Offline" Calls Between Landline Telephones - no Phone Network
items.description: In this video, I show how to create a standalone telephone system using two regular landline phones and a single analog telephone adaptor (ATA). The phones behave exactly like real telephones — you get a dial tone, ringing, and proper call connection — but everything works completely offline! This setup is perfect for making a on-stage telephone ring as a theatre prop, for escape rooms, museum or art exhibitions, intercoms or creative projects where you want a create a working phone call between two phones without needing a telephone network or the internet. And no hardware modifications or coding required :) I demonstrate the full configuration using a Grandstream HT-802 ATA, including how to set up internal dialing, optional auto-dial (intercom-style operation), and how to enable static IP so that the system runs completely standalone once configured. More details about all of the projects featured on this channel can be found at Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/c/playfultech And you can join the discussion on the Discord: https://discord.gg/nxH8uvAZ Timings 00:00:00 - 00:01:00 Introduction and Demonstration 00:01:01 - 00:04:16 Hardware 00:04:17 - 00:11:42 HT-802 Configuration 00:11:43 - 00:12:30 Wrapup

items.title: Automate any wireless device
items.description: Lots of electronic devices comes with remote controls - often designed as small keyfobs, these generally broadcast commands encoded as radio signals, broadcast on either 315MHz or 433MHz radio frequency. In this video, I'll explain how you can use a cheap RF receiver with an Arduino, ESP32, or other microcontroller to receive and learn the commands sent from these remote controls, identify and separate the control signal from the noise in the raw signal, and copy the encoding protocol used to perfectly clone the original. You can then re-broadcast that signal to add automation or "smart" control to any dumb device, such as triggering them via a network message or sensor. Perfect for smart homes or escape rooms! I'm using the RF433Any library from https://github.com/sebmillet/RF433any More details about all of the projects featured on this channel can be found at Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/c/playfultech And you can join the discussion on the Discord: https://discord.gg/jhSJfF7D Timings 00:00:00 - 00:00:57 Introduction and Demonstration 00:00:58 - 00:02:59 Why clone RF signals? 00:03:00 - 00:05:25 Capturing RF codes 00:05:26 00:07:05 Filtering noise 00:07:06 - 00:10:22 Retransmitting commands 00:10:23 - 00:12:46 Wrapup

items.title: Magic Glass (aka PDLC film, or "Smart Glass")
items.description: This is a video about Polymer Dispersed Liquid Crystal (PDLC) film - a clear sheet that normally has a milky white appearance which diffuses any light passing through it. When you apply a voltage across the two sides however, the crystals in the sheet align and the sheet instantly becomes transparent! It's trivial to use, and can be used for a whole range of interesting theatrical special effects, magic tricks, escape rooms, or other creative uses. To demonstrate it, I created a window created from a 4x3 array of PDLC panels, which were individually switchable from relays, controlled by an ESP32. I then added a 4x3 matrix keypad (read using a PCF8574 GPIO port expander) so that pressing any of the keypad buttons would toggle the opacity of the corresponding panels. You could use this to reveal a mechanism, a secret code, a set of symbols that needed to be matched in pairs (e.g. a memory "concentration" game), or many other ways... let me know what ideas you have for how it could be used! items.title: ESP32 Pneumatic Automatic Drawer Mechanism
items.description: It's nearly Halloween again, which is perfect timing for this spooky theatrical prop - a set of drawers that open and close by themselves! Using pneumatic cylinders controlled by an ESP32, you can make the drawers open when a sensor is activated, synchronise them in time to music or triggered by some other event, or activate them manually. I'll demonstrate a simple Bluetooth app I made which allows you to open and close the drawers remotely from a mobile phone app. Great for haunt attractions or theatre and, because they can be remotely closed, they're also ideal for use in an escape room as a set piece, or an alternative to maglocks that can be automatically reset at the end of the game! items.title: How to Create your own Biohazard Escape Room Puzzle
items.description: I made an escape room puzzle using three monitors to display live video feeds from inside a sand-blasting cabinet, in which players needed to insert their hands into protective gloves in order to solve a simple puzzle. It's a fun task, and the additional constraints of abstracting both the input and feedback mechanisms make it more challenging and interesting, whilst still it keeping it thematically-appropriate. In this video, I'll show you how I made it, but also how you can apply the same logic of apply layers of constraints, abstractions, and additional solving steps to turn any mundane task into a fun escape room puzzle! items.title: Pneumatics 101: A Beginner's Guide to Building Air-Powered Props
items.description: An introduction and demonstration of the components required to build a pneumatic system. Many of my previous projects have included moving parts powered by electricity - e.g. stepper motors, servos, linear actuators. But, using air-powered pneumatic cylinders can generate a different quality of motion, which is more powerful, more natural, and more organic - it's perfect for animatronic character movement, but also trap doors, reveals, or other theatrical special effects in escape rooms, haunted houses, or other themed attractions. I'll introduce the functionality of each of the main pneumatic components you'll need, and also draw comparisons to their equivalent component in an electrical circuit.
